root_cause.text: In the NFC NCI subsystem, nci_transceive() incorrectly assumed ownership handling on its early error returns and failed to free the caller-owned skb when rf_conn_info was missing, no active target was set, or NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE was already busy, causing a memory leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states “nci_transceive() takes ownership of the skb passed by the caller, but the -EPROTO, -EINVAL, and -EBUSY error paths return without freeing it,” and the patch adds kfree_skb(skb) immediately before each of those returns in net/nfc/nci/core.c.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In the NFC NCI subsystem, nci_transceive() incorrectly assumed ownership handling on its early error returns and failed to free the caller-owned skb when rf_conn_info was missing, no active target was set, or NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE was already busy, causing a memory leak.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explicitly states “nci_transceive() takes ownership of the skb passed by the caller, but the -EPROTO, -EINVAL, and -EBUSY error paths return without freeing it,” and the patch adds kfree_skb(skb) immediately before each of those returns in net/nfc/nci/core.c.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the skb on nci_transceive() early error paths to prevent memory leaks when data exchange cannot start.
intent_record.what: The change adds kfree_skb(skb) calls before each early return in nci_transceive() when ndev->rf_conn_info is NULL, when there is no active target protocol, and when NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE is already set, and wraps those return paths in braces where needed.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now frees the outgoing socket buffer on these error paths instead of returning immediately, preventing the skb from being leaked when transceive setup fails before the buffer is handed off for transmission.

grouping_result.intent: Free the skb on nci_transceive() early error paths to prevent memory leaks when data exchange cannot start.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it frees the caller-owned skb on nci_transceive() early error paths, fixing the memory leak when data exchange cannot start.

candidates.rationale: This early error return occurs when rf_conn_info is missing and exits without freeing the caller-owned skb, directly causing the memory leak described in the root cause.
This early error return is taken when no active target is set and returns before releasing the caller-owned skb, matching one of the leak paths in the root cause.
This early error return is hit when NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE is already busy; it returns without freeing skb, directly embodying the leak condition.

vuln_statements.explanation: This early return is taken when rf_conn_info is missing. In the pre-fix code, nci_transceive() exits here without freeing the caller-owned skb, causing the memory leak described in the root cause.
This early return occurs when no active target is set. The function returns before releasing the caller-owned skb, making this one of the direct leak paths identified in the root cause.
This early return is reached when NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE is already busy. Because the pre-fix code returns here without freeing the caller-owned skb, it directly causes the memory leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the full relevant early-return logic inside nci_transceive(). In this commit, the function adds a new early error path: `conn_info = nci_get_conn_info_by_conn_id(ndev, NCI_STATIC_RF_CONN_ID); if (!conn_info) return -EPROTO;`. This returns immediately without freeing the caller-owned `skb`. The root cause states that nci_transceive() leaked the skb on early error returns when `rf_conn_info` was missing, no active target was set, or `NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE` was already busy. This snippet clearly shows one of those vulnerable conditions in the new logical-connection form: missing connection info (`!conn_info`) causes an early return with no `kfree_skb(skb)`/`consume_skb(skb)` or equivalent cleanup. The later existing early returns also remain visible: `if (...) return -EBUSY;` likewise shows no skb free in this function body. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present. The fix is not present because none of the early returns shown perform skb cleanup before returning.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is `nci_data_exchange()`, and the root-cause vulnerability is specifically about `nci_transceive()` failing to free a caller-owned `skb` on early error paths when `rf_conn_info` is missing, no active target is set, or `NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE` is already busy. In this snippet, the relevant vulnerable function `nci_transceive()` is completely absent. The code shown only adds a busy check in `nci_data_exchange()` via `if (test_and_set_bit(NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE, &ndev->flags)) return -EBUSY;` and clears the bit on send failure. There is no `kfree_skb()`/`dev_kfree_skb()` or equivalent ownership handling here, and none of the root-cause conditions involving `rf_conn_info` or active target checks are present in this function body. diff --git a/net/nfc/nci/core.c b/net/nfc/nci/core.
bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in `nci_data_exchange()`, so the snippet is sufficient. The function takes a caller-provided `struct sk_buff *skb` and on the early error path it returns without freeing it: `if (!ndev->target_active_prot) { nfc_err("unable to exchange data, no active target"); return -EINVAL; }`. This matches the root cause pattern of early returns not releasing the caller-owned skb. The function then stores callback state and calls `return nci_send_data(ndev, ndev->conn_id, skb);`, but there is no cleanup on the visible early error case. There is also no fix present such as `kfree_skb(skb)` before returning on error, nor any ownership-transfer handling comment or helper that would consume the skb on failure. Therefore this initial implementation contains the vulnerable construct and does not yet include the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function is sufficient because it contains the relevant early-return ownership logic for `skb`. The root cause says `nci_transceive()` leaks the caller-owned `skb` on early error returns when no active target is set or when `NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE` is already busy. In this commit version, `nci_data_exchange()` has multiple early returns that do not free `skb`: `if (target_idx > ndev->n_targets) { return -EINVAL; }` and `if (test_and_set_bit(NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE, &ndev->flags)) return -EBUSY;`. The newly added busy check directly matches one of the vulnerable conditions from the root cause: on `-EBUSY`, the function returns without calling any `kfree_skb(skb)`-style cleanup. The added `clear_bit(NCI_DATA_EXCHANGE, &ndev->flags);` only handles flag cleanup after `nci_send_data()` failure and does not address skb lifetime on the early exits.
